svg.title: Decision 612's embedding layers: 43 feature vectors in, 43 vectors out
svg.desc: Decision 612 of the game of 5 November. Left, the input layer: 43 feature vectors, each drawn as a bar with a tick for every non-zero feature value at its column. The zones have 37 feature vectors of 42,532 inputs each, 840 non-zero feature values in all: shown are Shensi with 9, Hopeh 28, Suiyuan 12, Szechwan 2, Tsinghai 13, 31 more zones, and sea zone P14 with 86. The global features are 1 feature vector of 4,076 inputs with 176 non-zero feature values. The legal actions have 5 feature vectors of 12,627 inputs each, 80 non-zero feature values in all: the attacks on Hopeh, Suiyuan, Szechwan and Tsinghai with 19 each, and ending the phase with 4. Middle, the embedding layers: every zone feature vector goes through the zone embedding table, 42,532 embeddings of 64, the same weights for all 37 zones; the global feature vector through the global embedding table, 4,076 embeddings of 64; every action feature vector through the action embedding table, 12,627 embeddings of 64, the same weights for all 5 legal actions. Each feature vector goes through on its own. Right, the outputs: one vector of 64 numbers per feature vector, 43 in all: 37 zone vectors, 1 global vector and 5 action vectors. No embedding layer adds one feature vector to another; the vectors meet only in the layers after it.
svg.text: Decision 612's embedding layers: 43 feature vectors in, 43 vectors out
Each feature vector goes through its part's embedding layer on its own; those of one part share one embedding table. Ticks mark non-zero feature values.
ONE VECTOR OF 64 NUMBERS PER FEATURE VECTOR
Zone features: 37 feature vectors of 42,532 inputs each, 840 non-zero feature values in all
Global features: 1 feature vector of 4,076 inputs, 176 non-zero feature values
Action features: 5 feature vectors of 12,627 inputs each, 80 non-zero feature values in all
43 feature vectors in, 43 vectors out: 37 zone vectors, 1 global vector and 5 action vectors. No embedding layer adds one feature vector to another;
the vectors meet only in the layers after it (sections 6.4 to 6.8).
